back: The decline in the quality or productivity of land, water or ecosystems, usually caused by human activity.
Land degradation in arid, semi-arid and dry sub-humid areas caused by climatic variation and human activities.
Clearing vegetation, ploughing up and down slopes, overgrazing, cultivating steep land and stream banks.
Divert run-off from the gully head, build check dams to trap silt, plant grass and trees, fence out animals.
Contour ridges, terraces, mulching, conservation agriculture (minimum tillage, cover, rotation), vetiver strips.
Community knowledge and customs, such as totems, taboos and sacred forests, that protect natural resources.
Dams and canals lose storage, irrigation is reduced and aquatic life is harmed.
Backfill pits, spread stored topsoil, re-vegetate with local species, treat water and monitor.
Population pressure, poverty, lack of alternative fuel and land, and weak enforcement.
